message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several key rights under state law and local ordinances. Here’s a broad overview: | Category | Tenant Rights | |----------|---------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is for a longer period).
• Must return the deposit within 30 days after the tenancy ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear and tear. | | **Habitability** | • Landlords must keep the property safe, clean, and in good repair.
• Must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical systems, and structural integrity. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords must give reasonable notice (usually 24–48 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed but must be disclosed in writing. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written leases are required for residential rentals of more than one year.
• Tenants can terminate a lease early with proper notice (typically 30 days). | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the legal eviction process, which includes providing written notice and filing a lawsuit if necessary. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • In some cases, tenants may repair issues themselves and deduct costs from rent, though this is limited and requires following specific procedures. | These rights can vary slightly depending on whether you live in a city with its own housing ordinance (e.g., Austin, Dallas, Houston). For detailed guidance tailored to your situation, consider consulting a local attorney or tenant advocacy group.
